summary: DEF-028. Removes an impossible column lookup from stamp_portal_provenance(), which has raised 42703 on every portal write to invoices, bills, bank_transactions and receipts since the function was created. Re-issues one trigger function; no table, column, trigger, policy or grant is altered.

problem.mechanism: stamp_portal_provenance() resolved the writing contact by selecting a contact id off public.portal_access. That column does not exist, so the statement raises 42703 'column "contact_id" does not exist'.
problem.age: Authored broken. The identical statement is present in the creating migration 20260608112113 — it has never worked. This is not drift and not a regression from any recent release.
problem.why_it_survived: The function returns early for non-portal callers, so the broken statement is unreachable for accountant and staff writes. Only a portal session reaches it. It was found because the DEF-001/002 verification tried to exercise the portal invoice-create capability.
problem.blast_radius: Four BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE triggers, all enabled: trg_portal_provenance_invoices, trg_portal_provenance_bills, trg_portal_provenance_bank_tx, trg_portal_provenance_receipts.
problem.product_consequence: Portal invoice creation, bill creation, receipt upload and transaction explanation have NEVER worked end to end. The portal_visibility_settings capabilities allow_invoice_create, allow_bill_create, allow_receipt_upload and allow_transaction_explain have been unusable in practice regardless of how they were configured. This should be treated as a feature that has not shipped, not as a regression.

the_decision_not_taken.finding: There is NO correct column to substitute. No table in the schema links an authenticated user to a contacts row: portal_access carries user_id, client_id, company_id and role; contacts carries no user_id. stamp_portal_provenance is also the ONLY function in the database that references created_by_contact_id, so there is no established resolution pattern to copy.
the_decision_not_taken.chosen: v_contact is left explicitly NULL and the audit metadata records contact_attribution = 'unresolved_no_portal_contact_link', so the gap is visible in the audit trail rather than indistinguishable from a genuine absence.
the_decision_not_taken.why_this_loses_nothing: Because the lookup always raised, created_by_contact_id has never been populated on any row. Nothing that works today is lost. Actor attribution remains durable: bookkeeping_audit_log.actor_id records auth.uid(), and created_by_portal / source = 'portal' still mark provenance. The COALESCE is kept so an explicitly supplied value still wins and so populating v_contact later needs no other change.
the_decision_not_taken.explicitly_rejected: Matching a portal user to a contact by email or name. Identity by name-match is forbidden by the governance design (2026-07-22-data-governance-architecture-design.md, owner-confirmed decision 2). It would attribute writes to the wrong person, which is worse than NULL. A test guards that no such matching is introduced.
the_decision_not_taken.OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED: Should portal_access carry a real contact FK, so portal writes can be attributed to a named person? That is a product decision about the portal identity model — today a portal login is bound to a client/company, not to a contact. It is NOT required to close this outage and is deliberately not bundled here. If the answer is yes it needs its own increment: the column, a backfill rule that does not rely on name or email matching, and the trigger change to consume it.

authoring_method: The body was extracted from the LIVE definition (md5 f67d2205) and edited programmatically against asserted anchors — the script fails if an anchor is missing or matches more than once. Exactly two edits: the lookup statement replaced with an explicit NULL assignment plus the reasoning, and the audit metadata gaining the contact_attribution marker. Nothing else retyped or reordered. Triggers are untouched; replacing a function body leaves its attachments in place.

expected_objects.object: stamp_portal_provenance no longer executes the impossible lookup
expected_objects.verify_via: pg_proc.prosrc for stamp_portal_provenance contains no 'INTO v_contact FROM'. Matched on the statement rather than the table name, which still appears in the body comment. Asserted in-migration; confirm independently.
expected_objects.evidence: CONFIRMED TWICE, independently. Executor pre-apply reproduction raised: ERROR: column "contact_id" does not exist / QUERY: SELECT contact_id FROM public.portal_access ... / CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function stamp_portal_provenance() line 14. Post-apply the reviewing party read the live body via mcp_list_functions on 2026-08-05: 'INTO v_contact FROM' is absent, 'v_contact := NULL;' is present with the reasoning retained, and definition_hash moved f67d2205 -> fa023bbb.

expected_objects.object: A portal user can create an invoice
expected_objects.verify_via: THE PROOF-OF-REPAIR CASE. Reproduce the failure FIRST: as a portal user holding allow_invoice_create, create an invoice and confirm 42703 pre-apply. After apply the same write must succeed, with created_by_portal = true, source = 'portal', and created_by_contact_id NULL. Requires a portal session — the same fixture the DEF-001/002 receipt needs.
expected_objects.evidence: Executor, in a rolled-back transaction: portal invoice created successfully with created_by_portal=t, source=portal, created_by_contact_id NULL. This is the defect closing — the same write raised 42703 pre-apply.

expected_objects.object: Portal writes work on all four tables carrying the trigger
expected_objects.verify_via: Repeat a portal write against bills, receipts and bank_transactions. bank_transactions takes the UPDATE branch (updated_by_portal) rather than the INSERT branch, so it must be exercised separately — it is the one path with different behaviour.
expected_objects.evidence: invoices PASS, bills PASS (created_by_portal=t, source=portal), receipts PASS. bank_transactions NOT exercised end to end: the trigger provably fired — the failing row's DETAIL shows source=portal and updated_by_portal=t — but the insert hit an unrelated bank_account_id NOT NULL violation, and sandbox_exec holds no UPDATE grant on that table, so the UPDATE branch (the only branch that table takes) could not be driven. The trigger firing and setting both columns is strong evidence the branch works; it is not proof.

expected_objects.object: review_status is still forced to pending_review where configured
expected_objects.verify_via: With portal_visibility_settings.client_bookkeeping_mode = 'review_required' (or the per-table require_review_* flag set), a portal INSERT must land with review_status = 'pending_review'. This is the responsibility most at risk from a body replacement and must not be assumed from the diff.
expected_objects.evidence: Only one portal_visibility_settings row exists org-wide and it is 'operational'. sandbox_exec has no UPDATE on that table, so it could not be flipped to 'review_required' to drive the branch. The executor flagged this rather than claiming it, which is the correct call. Unverified — the review-gating path is untested on LIVE.

expected_objects.object: bookkeeping_audit_log records the write, marked unresolved
expected_objects.verify_via: After a portal write, the new bookkeeping_audit_log row must carry actor_id = the portal user, actor_role = 'portal', and metadata.contact_attribution = 'unresolved_no_portal_contact_link'.
expected_objects.evidence: Executor: bookkeeping_audit_log row written with actor_role=portal and metadata contact_attribution=unresolved_no_portal_contact_link. Independently corroborated by the reviewing party reading the live body, which builds exactly that marker.

expected_objects.object: Staff writes still take the early return and are unchanged
expected_objects.verify_via: As an organisation member, create an invoice. It must succeed with created_by_portal false and no bookkeeping_audit_log row from this trigger. This path was never broken and must stay that way.
expected_objects.evidence: Executor, no JWT claim: created_by_portal=f, source=accountant, no audit row. The early return for non-portal callers is intact.

expected_objects.object: All four attachments survive the replace and stay enabled
expected_objects.verify_via: pg_trigger: exactly 4 non-internal, non-disabled triggers point at stamp_portal_provenance. Asserted in-migration.
expected_objects.evidence: Executor: 4 non-internal, non-disabled triggers bound to stamp_portal_provenance.

migrations.rollback_note: No rollback script. Reverting reinstates a function that raises 42703 on every portal write — fix-forward only. The prior body is recoverable from 20260608112113 and from live def-hash f67d2205 if ever needed.

steps: Apply 20260803140000_def_028_portal_provenance_contact_link.sql. Self-verifying: a DO block asserts the end state before COMMIT, including that all four triggers survive, so a partial apply aborts.
Reproduce the failure FIRST with a portal session — a portal invoice create must return 42703 pre-apply.
After apply, re-run that write and confirm it succeeds.
Exercise bills, receipts and bank_transactions too; bank_transactions takes the other branch.
Confirm review gating still forces pending_review where configured — this is the responsibility most at risk.
Confirm an accountant write is still unaffected.
Refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version.
Report back so I can complete this receipt.
Then the portal-capability check on docs/releases/pending/2026-07-31-def-001-002.json becomes runnable for the first time — it was blocked by this defect.

guarded_by: src/test/regression/def-028-portal-provenance.test.ts — 11 static guards. The lookup detector was run against the LIVE broken body and matches, so it catches the defect rather than merely passing on the fix. Guards also assert the repair is a removal and not a truncation, that no email/name identity matching is introduced, and that the migration touches no trigger or table.

hash_recording_correction.reported: The executor recorded live pre-apply md5(prosrc) = d230bd4e…, not the f67d2205 this receipt carried, and flagged it as a possible discrepancy.
hash_recording_correction.resolution: NOT a discrepancy — the two hash DIFFERENT INPUTS. f67d2205e089b92c6603834d46f467d1 is md5(pg_get_functiondef(oid)), which is what mcp_list_functions returns as `definition_hash` (see 20260722181057). That covers the full CREATE FUNCTION text including the signature, LANGUAGE, SECURITY DEFINER and SET search_path clauses. The executor measured md5(prosrc), which is the function BODY alone. Both are correct measurements of the same broken function, and the executor independently confirmed the broken lookup was present verbatim.
hash_recording_correction.defect_in_this_receipt: Recording a pg_get_functiondef hash while instructing the verifier to check prosrc is a documentation defect that manufactures exactly this false alarm. Corrected here, and both values are now stated with their source expression.

verification_status_2026_08_05: 5 of 7 expected objects PASS. One is PARTIAL (bank_transactions UPDATE branch) and one is NOT EXERCISED (review gating). Convention section 3 forbids applied-verified unless every check passes, so this receipt REMAINS in pending/ despite the migration being live and the reported defect being closed. What is settled: the 42703 that broke every portal write since June is gone, confirmed by two parties reading LIVE independently. What is not: two branches that could not be driven because sandbox_exec lacks the UPDATE grants needed to set up their fixtures. Both are fixture-access limitations, not evidence of a fault.
follow_up_from_verification: sandbox_exec cannot UPDATE bank_transactions or portal_visibility_settings, so two branches of a trigger on four tables cannot be verified on LIVE by the party applying the change. That is a verification-capability gap, and it will recur on every future change to this trigger. Either grant the exec role the narrow UPDATE it needs, or provide seeded fixtures for the portal paths — the Phase 0 section 4 fixture work already approved.
bank_transactions inserts require bank_account_id NOT NULL, which the executor hit while constructing a fixture. Worth confirming the portal path always supplies it.

Whether portal_access should carry a real contact FK remains an open product decision. Until it does, created_by_contact_id is permanently NULL on portal writes and the audit trail records contact_attribution=unresolved_no_portal_contact_link. Actor attribution is unaffected — bookkeeping_audit_log.actor_id still records auth.uid().
